elements.title: NASA astronaut and Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman training in the Neutral Buoyancy Lab
elements.content: Shows NASA astronaut and Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman in an orange spacesuit floating in water during training beside a spacecraft mockup, with another suited person behind him. Printed caption: “NASA astronaut and Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman participates in training Jan. 23 in the Neutral Buoyancy Lab at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.” Photo credit: “PHOTO CREDIT – NASA Johnson Space Center”

elements.title: The Cygnus space freighter fires its engine to raise the station’s orbital altitude
elements.content: Shows the Northrop Grumman Cygnus space freighter firing its engine in space, with star trails and aurora visible. Printed caption: “The Cygnus space freighter fires its engine to raise the station’s orbital altitude” “This long-duration photograph taken with a station camera uses increased sensitivity and shows the Northrop Grumman Cygnus space freighter firing its engine to raise the International Space Station’s orbital altitude. The reboosts counteract atmospheric drag and prepare for the space station upcoming spacecraft activities. The orbital outpost was soaring 263 miles above the Indian Ocean with a field of star trails above and the Aurora Australis below.” Photo credit: “PHOTO CREDIT – NASA Johnson”

OTHER INFORMATION
CIVIL MONETARY PENALTY ADJUSTMENT FOR INFLATION
Civil Monetary Penalty Adjustment for Inflation
For The Fiscal Year Ended September 30, 2024
The Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015 (P.L. 114-74), requires agencies to make 
annual inflation adjustments to civil monetary penalties and report on these adjustments in their AFR.
Agencies must include, as Other Information, information about civil monetary penalties within their jurisdiction and 
the annual inflation adjustments made under the Act.
NASA reviewed each of the penalty amounts under its statutes and penalty amounts for inflation when required under 
law. The authorities imposing the penalties, the civil penalties, the adjustment years, and the current penalty amounts 
for penalty updates are located in the Federal Register Volume 89, No. 56 at govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-03-21/
pdf/2024-05999.pdf.
Did You Know?
NASA astronaut and Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman participates in training Jan. 23 in the Neutral Buoyancy Lab at the agency’s Johnson 
Space Center in Houston.
 NASA Johnson Space Center
PHOTO CREDIT —
The Cygnus space freighter fires its engine to raise the station's orbital altitude
This long-duration photograph taken with a station camera uses increased sensitivity and shows the Northrop 
Grumman Cygnus space freighter firing its engine to raise the International Space Station's orbital altitude. The 
reboosts counteract atmospheric drag and prepare for the space station upcoming spacecraft activities. The orbital 
outpost was soaring 263 miles above the Indian Ocean with a field of star trails above and the Aurora Australis below.
PHOTO CREDIT — NASA Johnson
